title: Legal Chair Positioning Reps
description: Players practise getting legally positioned with the chair set before contact arrives, learning exactly what separates a legal position from an illegal block in wheelchair basketball's contact rules.

content.objective: Get legally positioned with the chair fully set before contact, understanding what makes it legal.
content.setup: A driver attacks the lane as a help defender gets into position ahead of them.
instructions: The help defender gets the chair fully stopped and positioned before the driver arrives.
The driver attacks at a controlled, game-realistic pace, not full-contact speed.
The group discusses together whether the position was set early enough and square.
Repeat with the defender arriving late to show the contrast.
coachingPoints: Get the chair completely stopped and square well before contact.
Front casters should be straight, not turned, for a legal set position.
Take the contact without being knocked backward out of position.
commonMistakes: Still moving or turning the chair at the moment of contact.
Setting the position too late, after the driver has already committed.
Reaching with the hands instead of using chair position.
content.safety: Run this drill at a controlled pace with light, safe contact only; stop immediately if contact becomes too forceful.
